device.name: Drobo NAS (FS / 5N / 5N2 / B800fs) — status daemon
device.notes:
Drobo's parent StorCentric filed Chapter 11 in June 2022, Drobo ended sales on 27 January 2023 (support became self-service), and the company went into Chapter 7 liquidation that spring. Drobo Dashboard, the desktop app owners used to see drive health, is unsupported and its support site no longer resolves. The NAS units themselves keep running their BeyondRAID arrays, and the daemon behind Dashboard still answers on the LAN.
That daemon pushes the whole array status to anyone who connects: open TCP 5000 and, with no request, no login and no TLS, the NAS sends a 16-byte header and an XML document describing the array, its capacity and every drive slot, and sends it again every 10-20 seconds for as long as the socket stays open. That is enough for a phone or a monitor to show the traffic-light status of each bay, warn on a failing or missing drive, and track free space — the jobs Dashboard did — without any Drobo software.
This spec is READ-ONLY on purpose. nasd also listens on TCP 5001 and UDP 5002. Strings in the daemon binary show a command set that includes destructive drive-management verbs alongside status getters, presumably reachable on one of those ports; nothing about it is publicly documented and it is left out.

openness.notes: Never published by Drobo. The XML is self-describing enough that the droboports community documented it in the DroboFS days; the binary header in front of it was written down later from one 5N2.

credentials.notes: No authentication on port 5000. Anyone on the LAN can read the status document, which includes drive serials and the unit's serial.

factory_reset.description: Drobo units do have reset procedures (network settings and full resets), but none applies to reading status, and the ones that erase the disk pack are catastrophic. Nothing is transcribed here.
factory_reset.effect: Not established for the status daemon, which holds no client state. A Drobo reset that wipes the disk pack destroys the data on it and is never needed to read status.

methods.description: Open TCP 5000 on the NAS and read one frame: a 16-byte header, then the XML body whose length the header gives.
methods.name: Connect and read

steps.action: Connect the NAS to the LAN by Ethernet and note its address.
Open a TCP connection to port 5000. Send nothing.
steps.expect: A frame beginning DRINASD arrives at once (the reference script allows up to 20 seconds).

steps.action: Read 16 header bytes, then the body length from bytes 12-15 (big-endian), then the body; close the socket or keep it open for updates.

setup.notes: Nothing to enable: the status daemon runs whenever the NAS is up and on the network. The NAS's own first-time setup was done with Drobo Dashboard, which is no longer distributed; a unit that has already been set up keeps its configuration.

rejoin.notes: Wired Ethernet; the NAS takes its address by DHCP unless set static in Dashboard.

testing.notes: Not read from hardware by this project. The XML element set comes from the droboports wiki and agrees with two exporters; the 16-byte frame header rests on one 5N2 write-up that itself publishes no capture or hex dump (the two exporters skip the header by searching for the XML start).

entities.name: Array Status
entities.notes: mStatus from the pushed document, mapped through payload_formats.ArrayStatus.

entities.name: Bay Status
entities.notes: One per bay: each <nX> record's mStatus mapped through payload_formats.SlotStatus.

evidence.documentation_review: The droboports wiki pages and three community tools (jerimiah797's protocol notes and script, drobo_exporter, drobomon) were read on 2026-10-11. They agree on port 5000, the push behaviour and the XML element names. The status tables are from droboports, plus one array code from drobo_exporter.
evidence.open_questions: The 16-byte header layout rests on one source, jerimiah797's reading of one 5N2 (firmware 4.3.1), which publishes no capture; the FS, 5N and B810n are unverified, and the 10-20 s repeat cadence is the wiki's (FS/5N era) and unobserved on a 5N2. The UDP 5002 discovery payload and the TCP 5001 command channel are undocumented.

http_endpoints.description: Placeholder only, to satisfy the schema's access-surface rule. The status is pushed over a raw TCP socket on port 5000 (see protocol_details.nasd_frame), not HTTP.
http_endpoints.name: Local API Placeholder

ArrayStatus.description: Overall mStatus. Values from the droboports wiki, some marked "possibly" there. The low bits behave like flags (0x0004 yellow, 0x0002 red, 0x0010 bad drive, 0x0040 removed, 0x0200 relayout, 0x10000 no free slot / critical) but no source says so; match whole values first.

values.32774: Over the red capacity threshold, with empty slots (0x8006)
values.98310: Over red threshold with no empty slots (0x18006)
values.98320: Has bad drives (0x18010; from drobo_exporter's table)
values.98880: Relayout with redundancy critical; do not remove any drive (0x18240)

ESATMUpdate.description: The XML body. Root element <ESATMUpdate>; every value is the text of a child element. Capacities are in bytes.

fields.description: Unit serial (also mESAID). On the FS the first character is replaced with 0.
fields.name: mSerial

fields.description: Model name, when present. The droboports prose calls it empty and FS-only, but the wiki's own 5N firmware 3.2.0 sample carries 'Drobo 5N' and a 5N2 reports it; treat it as optional.
fields.name: mModel

fields.description: Used-space warning threshold in hundredths of a percent (8500 = 85.00 %).
fields.name: mYellowThreshold

fields.description: Counts down while data protection rebuilds; 0 when idle.
fields.name: mRelayoutCount

fields.description: Redundancy mode: 6 single, 7 dual; 4 seen, meaning unknown.
fields.name: mFirmwareFeatureStates

fields.description: Reported slot count: 8 on the FS and 6 on the 5N/5N2 (the sixth being the mSATA accelerator bay). Not always the number of <nX> records: FS firmware 1.2.6 reports 8 here but sends five records, so count the records themselves.
fields.name: mSlotCountExp

parse_rules: Read the frame per protocol_details.nasd_frame, drop the trailing NUL, then parse the XML.
Slots are under <mSlotsExp> as <n0>, <n1>, ... ; n0 is the top bay. Each slot record is a SlotRecord.
Read numbers as integers; capacities exceed 32 bits.
mTemperature in slot records is always 0; do not show it.

fields.description: Drive size; 0 when the bay is empty.
fields.name: mPhysicalCapacity

fields.description: Read as a percentage, which is an assumption: the wiki records it as 100 for HDDs and SSDs alike and 0 for an empty bay, and 5N and later only.
fields.name: SSDLifeRemaining

SlotStatus.description: Per-bay mStatus, with the colour the bay LED shows.

values.1: Red: array over 95 % full, add or replace a drive
values.4: Flashing green/yellow: relayout in progress, do not remove

nasd_frame.body: UTF-8 XML of exactly `length` bytes. The last byte is 0x00 and is counted in the length; strip it before parsing.
nasd_frame.cadence: Pushed once on connect and then every 10-20 s while the socket stays open.
header: offset 0, 8 bytes: magic, ASCII DRINASD followed by 0x00. Older firmware put a version character in byte 7 (DRINASD9 on DroboFS, DRINASDa on 5N); match the first seven bytes.
offset 12, 4 bytes: body length, unsigned 32-bit BIG-endian.
nasd_frame.other_ports: TCP 5001 and UDP 5002 also belong to nasd; undocumented, out of scope, and possibly destructive.

remaining_unknowns: Frame header layout confirmed on a single 5N2 (firmware 4.3.1); other models and older firmware may differ (older markers DRINASD9 / DRINASDa).
Whether the overall mStatus is a bitfield; the flag reading is inferred from the value table.
Discovery: UDP 5002 broadcasts are likely Dashboard's discovery channel, payload undocumented.
The B810n is assumed to run the same nasd; no source covers it.
A raw pushed TCP stream has no schema binding for entity state; the entities above name their XML elements in notes.
